paper.core_task: Analyzing gating mechanisms in softmax attention for language model training

contributions.name: Systematic investigation of gating positions in self-attention
contributions.author_claim_text: In this work, we investigate gating mechanisms in the standard softmax attention... we introduce gating at distinct positions
contributions.description: A comprehensive empirical study of gating placement at five distinct positions within the multi-head attention layer, analyzing their impact on performance.

contributions.name: Analysis of gating's effect on non-linearity and sparsity
contributions.author_claim_text: We identify two factors contributing to the efficacy of gating: (i) Non-Linearity... (ii) Sparsity.
contributions.description: An analysis revealing that gating effectiveness stems from introducing non-linearity between low-rank linear layers and creating input-dependent sparsity in SDPA outputs.

contributions.name: Elimination of attention sink phenomenon via gating
contributions.author_claim_text: Sparse gating eliminates the massive activation and attention sink... these models demonstrate superior performance in length generalization.
contributions.description: Demonstration that sparse, query-dependent gating at the SDPA output eliminates attention sinks and massive activations, improving training stability and long-context generalization.

novelty_claims.text: The specific study has the potential to separate itself from previous works in the area.
This claim is too broad, the impact of gating has been explored in linear attention [1] and standard attention [2,3] networks.
Proposed analysis is novel and makes a lot of sense.
